rules.identifiers: Tenant-owned object keys use opaque UUIDs. Never put organization names, user names, email addresses, phone numbers, lead names or original filenames in an S3 key.
rules.authorization: The backend must authorize organization, project and user ownership before issuing a short-lived presigned URL. A key prefix is not an authorization boundary by itself.
rules.database: PostgreSQL owns display names, MIME type, byte size, checksum, ownership and entity relationships. S3 stores bytes and operational manifests only.
rules.uploads: New uploads enter temporary/ or quarantine/ and move to a canonical tenant prefix only after validation.
rules.deletion: Database deletion and S3 deletion must use the stored opaque object key; never reconstruct a key from user-provided names.

prefixes.organizations/{organizationId}/shared/{a: Organization-owned files not tied to a project
prefixes.organizations/{organizationId}/projects/: Candidate evidence retained for an approved Discovery workflow
prefixes.organizations/{organizationId}/users/{us: Organization-owned files scoped to a member
prefixes.users/{userId}/files/{assetId}/original: Private user files not owned by an organization
prefixes.users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/file: User-owned project files where no organization owner exists
prefixes.temporary/{uploadId}: Unfinalized uploads; expires after one day
prefixes.quarantine/{uploadId}: Rejected or suspicious uploads; expires after fourteen days
prefixes.exports/{exportId}: Temporary GDPR or administrative exports; expires after seven days
prefixes.migration/{source}/{migrationItemId}: Migration staging retained until explicitly finalized
prefixes._system/storage-layout.json: Authoritative storage layout and privacy contract
